specific_rules: Steel angles and plates to be NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted in design documents.
Channels to be NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Steel W shapes (I sections) and tees to be NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Structural steel shall conform to the requirements listed on the Structural General Notes for each area and phase.
For each individual structure or component, steel subgrade shall be documented in the steel subcontractor’s information.
Selection of steel subgrade for connection fittings and subcontractor-designed items shall follow NBN EN 1993-1-10 with Belgian National Annex and applicable guidance.

Steel subcontractor shall liaise with the Structural Engineer of Record where subcontractor’s detailing or fabrication practice is not compatible with indicative subgrade information in Structural General Notes.
Steel sections for metal fabrications to conform to EN 10025.
Steel sections for stair stringers and other stair framing to conform to EN 10025.
Hollow structural sections to be NBN EN 10210 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Hot finished structural hollow sections for metal fabrications to conform to EN 10210.
Hollow sections for stairs, ramps, ladders and guards to conform to EN 10210 and/or ISO 10799 as applicable to member type.

materials.category: Cold-Formed and Sheet Steel for Decking and Fabrications
specific_rules: Steel deck units and sheet accessories shall be produced from galvanized steel sheet conforming to NBN EN 10346 and NBN EN 10143, Grade of Steel S350 unless otherwise indicated or agreed.
Deck units shall be free of dirt, rust, rolling oils and any materials detrimental to bond of field-applied finishes.
Roof deck shall be wide-rib units with no stiffening ribs on the top surface.
Plates for metal fabrications shall conform to ISO 3574 and ISO 6317.
Ungalvanized hot-rolled steel sheet for stairs/guards to conform to ISO 4995.
Ungalvanized cold-rolled steel sheet for stairs/guards to conform to ISO 4997.
Hot-rolled twin-roll cast carbon steel sheet for stairs/guards to conform to ISO 15177.
Cold-reduced steel sheets for general metal fabrications shall comply with ISO 3574 unless otherwise stated.
Steel pipe for barrier rails and similar fabrications shall conform to ISO 4200.
Plain end steel tubes, welded or seamless, for stairs, handrails and guards shall conform to ISO 4200.
Structural tubing for handrails and guards to comply with ISO 10799 for cold-formed welded structural hollow sections of non-alloy and fine grain steels.
Nominal diameters for handrails and guards: handrails 32 mm, guard top rails and infill rails 50 mm as specified for metal stairs and ramps.

materials.grade_or_type: Grade 8.8 / EN ISO 898 / NBN EN 14399 / NBN EN 15048
specific_rules: Bolts, nuts and washers for structural framing to conform to NBN EN 1090, Grade 8.8 unless noted otherwise.
High strength bolts shall conform to NBN EN 1993 and NBN EN 14399 for structural bolted assemblies.
Direct tension indicators shall meet the requirements of NBN EN 14399 and be used for slip-critical bolted connections for moment connections and bracing.
Washers in general shall conform to NBN EN 1993.
Washers in contact with high-strength bolt heads and nuts shall conform to NBN EN 14399.
Bevelled washers shall be square, smooth and sloped to ensure contact surfaces of bolt head and nut are parallel.
Anchor bolts for structural steel framing shall conform to NBN EN 15048, grade as specified in design documents, and be non-headed type unless otherwise indicated.
Bolts, nuts and washers for metal fabrications shall conform to EN ISO 898 and be zinc-coated for exterior use or where built into exterior walls.
All bolts shall be new and not re-used.
High-strength threaded fasteners for principal bolted connections shall be provided except where unfinished bolts are explicitly indicated.
Unfinished threaded fasteners shall be used only for secondary framing connections taking nominal stresses and temporary bracing.

materials.grade_or_type: Per EN 1011; NBN EN 1090; NBN EN ISO 9606-1; NBN EN ISO 14732
specific_rules: Welding materials for structural steel framing shall conform to NBN EN 1090 and associated codes for welding consumables, appropriate to parent metal.
Electrodes for structural steel framing shall conform to relevant standards referenced in NBN EN 1993-1-8 Group 5.
Welding materials for metal fabrications shall conform to EN 1011 requirements.
Welders for structural steel framing shall be qualified in accordance with NBN EN ISO 9606-1 within previous 12 months.
Welding operators and weld setters for mechanized and automatic welding of decking and other works shall be qualified in accordance with NBN EN ISO 14732.
Welders for steel decking (including shear studs and deck welds) shall be qualified per relevant European Welding Association standards.

Shear stud connectors for structural steel framing shall be proprietary type with minimum yield strength 350 N/mm2, minimum ultimate tensile strength 450 N/mm2, and minimum elongation 15%, complying with BS EN ISO 13918.
Stud shear connectors used with steel decking shall be proprietary type with the same mechanical property requirements and conform to EN ISO 13918.
Shear connectors shall be shop-welded to beams/girders using automatic end welding per manufacturer’s printed instructions.

Steel surfaces for shear connectors shall be prepared per connector manufacturer’s recommendations; top flanges must be free from mill scale, rust, grease, oil, paint and other substances detrimental to welding.
Weld studs through to primary steel members below through the deck where specified.

materials.grade_or_type: Rust-inhibitive primers; inorganic zinc-rich primers; alkyd primers
specific_rules: Shop and touch-up primer for structural steel shall be fabricator’s standard grey rust-inhibitive primer that complies with VOC limitations of the authorities having jurisdiction.
Touch-up primer for galvanized surfaces shall be fabricator’s standard compatible primer, complying with VOC limitations.
Members exposed to exterior outside a controlled building environment shall receive inorganic zinc-rich primer with minimum 60% volume solids, producing at least 85% metallic zinc in the dry film.
Surfaces receiving intumescent fireproofing shall be shop painted with heavy duty alkyd primer compatible with the intumescent system.
Shop primer for metal fabrications shall be grey metal primer or approved equal applied to minimum 50 microns DFT.
Touch-up primer for galvanized steel fabrications shall comply with EN ISO 17463 guidance for anticorrosive coatings.
All coating materials must be recommended by their manufacturers for the particular surface and exposure conditions and be mutually compatible.

materials.grade_or_type: Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003 / FX6002 systems
specific_rules: Intumescent coatings shall be factory-mixed thin film systems for spray application to primary and secondary structural steel members to achieve specified fire resistance ratings.

System 1 (Solvent-based, internal steelwork C1, off-site): Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003 intumescent basecoat with DFT sufficient to achieve fire resistance; FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer at nominal 25 microns DFT per EN ISO 12944-5; FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish top sealer at nominal 50 microns DFT per EN ISO 12944-5.

System 2 (Solvent-based, internal steelwork C1, off-site): Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX6002 ultra fast drying intumescent basecoat with DFT sufficient to achieve fire resistance; FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer at nominal 25 microns DFT per EN ISO 12944-5; FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish top sealer at nominal 50 microns DFT per EN ISO 12944-5.

Under certain circumstances, FIRETEX FX2003 may be applied directly to blast-cleaned steel prepared to a minimum Sa 2½ per EN ISO 8501-1 with surface profile 50–100 microns; this is subject to confirmation from the manufacturer’s technical department.
A/E of Record shall adjust DFT makeup of primer, intumescent basecoat and top sealer for alternate environment classes (e.g., C2, C3, C4) as required by EN ISO 12944-5 and project conditions.
Intumescent coating systems shall be tested in accordance with EN 13381-4 and classified per EN 13501 for required fire resistance periods.
Intumescent coatings shall be compatible with underlying primers and any topcoat systems; compatibility shall be documented by manufacturer’s certificates.
Grout for structural steel base plates shall be non-shrink, non-metallic aggregate type.
Grout shall be capable of developing minimum compressive strength of 35 MPa at 28 days.
Grout formulation and installation shall follow Structural General Notes and manufacturer’s instructions.
Grout shall be used solidly between column plates and bearing surfaces, trowelled smooth and splayed neatly to 45 degrees.
Shrink-resistant or non-shrink grout submittals shall be provided as part of structural steel submittals.

materials.grade_or_type: Edge strips, closure strips, sump pans, fillers (steel sheet)
specific_rules: Provide minimum 1.6 mm thick slab edge pour stops, edge strips, closure strips and sump pans for steel decking interfaces.
Provide minimum 0.8 mm thick fillers, ridge and valley plates and sheet metal closures at openings between floor units, at columns, penetrations and where deck cells change direction.
Provide necessary supplementary framing for deck support at columns and at openings up to and including 450 mm.
Mechanical fasteners and sidelap connectors may be Hilti or other approved alternative, subject to diaphragm design calculations and approvals.
Closures and accessories shall be adequately connected to framing steel and adjacent deck units to provide continuous support and closure.

materials.category: Metal Fabrications (Ladders, Barriers, Angles, Guards, Canopies)
materials.grade_or_type: Carbon steel to EN 10025 / EN 10210 / ISO 4200 / ISO 10799
specific_rules: Steel ladders shall be fabricated in compliance with Section 05 51 00; galvanised after fabrication.
Ladder side rails/stiles shall be manufacturer’s standard steel flat bar with eased edges, spaced at maximum 600 mm; single stile not prohibited.
Ladder rungs shall be 20–50 mm rectangular steel with maximum 600 mm clear width, fitted into side rails, plug welded and ground smooth on outer faces.
Vertical spacing of ladder rungs shall be 225–300 mm, consistent within a flight; maximum 6 m height before intermediate landing is required.
Provide minimum 175 mm clearance from wall to ladder rung centerline.
Support ladders at top, bottom and intermediate points not more than 1500 mm apart using welded or bolted steel brackets designed for adequate support and 175 mm minimum wall clearance.
Extend ladder rails at least 1100 mm above top rung and return rails to wall or structure; where adjacent structure is lower, goose-neck rails back to the structure to provide secure access.
Provide safety cage hoops above 3 m from finished floor level where shown, in compliance with EN ISO 14122.
Barrier rails shall use 40 mm diameter steel pipe and steel channel sections with galvanized finish.
Ledge angles, shelf angles, channels and plates not attached to structural framing for support of metal decking shall be galvanized.
Roof opening framing shall be provided as detailed with prime paint or galvanized finish; frames are required for openings 300 mm by 300 mm or larger.

Concrete edge confinement angles shall be galvanized steel angles with integral anchor bolts welded using 2.5 mm full perimeter fillet welds, drilled and tapped for 6 mm machine screws, and with anchorages spaced not greater than 1200 mm on center and not closer than 100 mm from ends and corners.
Downspout (downpipe) guards and cantilevered canopy supports shall be galvanized steel as detailed.

All external and exposed metal fabrications and associated components shall be factory prefinished to a corrosion protection level suitable for a C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012.

materials.category: Metal Stairs, Ramps, Handrails and Guards
materials.grade_or_type: Carbon steel and aluminium components per EN 10025, ISO 4200, ISO 10799
specific_rules: Metal stairs shall include landing platforms, vertical and horizontal supports, railings and guards, fabricated for anchorage to each other and building structure.
Stair assemblies shall support uniform live load of 500 kg/m² and a concentrated load of 150 kg on 2580 mm² area with deflection of stringer or landing framing not exceeding span/360.
Exit stair towers shall be designed for stacking as self-supporting structures to full building height where required.
Structural design of stair and railing assemblies must comply with applicable local codes and the most stringent European or local regulations.

Top rail of guardrail shall resist nominal 1.0 kN/m uniformly applied load in any direction at top, and 0.5 kN concentrated load in any direction at any point; uniform and concentrated loads need not act concurrently.
Guardrail infill area shall resist horizontal uniform load of 1.0 kN/m² and point load 0.5 kN; these loads need not be combined with top rail loads.
Metal jointing and finish quality level for visible stair components shall be ‘Commercial’: joints inconspicuous, underside of stair not covered by soffit is considered exposed.
Exposed welded joints shall be ground smooth and flush; intermittent welds on back side shall be filled with body putty and sanded smooth.
Mechanical joints shall be butted tight, flush, hairline; bolts exposed to view shall be countersunk flat or oval head with no exposed nuts.
Exposed edges and corners shall be eased to a small uniform radius.
Metal surfaces to be painted/galvanised shall be sanded or ground smooth suitable for satin or matte finish.

Stairs with pan treads: metal pans 2 mm thick minimum, 50 mm deep minimum, welded to carrier angles welded to stringers; closed risers with same material and thickness as treads; riser nosings sloped with rounded nosing, depth overhang not more than 25 mm, nosing return flush with finished tread and not more than 12.5 mm wide.

Alternative stair treads may be galvanized or aluminium checker plate (Durbar or similar), 3 mm thick minimum, welded to carrier angles with additional support profiles as required by structural calculations.
Stringers for stairs and ramps shall be rolled steel channels 300 mm deep; ramp stringers shall have flange width 75 mm.
Landings shall match construction of treads or ramp surfaces, supported and reinforced to meet design load capacity.
Stairs and landings at electrical platforms shall be fabricated with bolted connections that permit removal and replacement for equipment maintenance.
Bridge-style roof stepovers shall be bigfoot-mounted and designed for height and wind loads in accordance with EN 14122.
Handrails shall be round steel pipe 32 mm nominal diameter unless otherwise indicated.
Guardrail top rails shall be round steel pipe or tube 50 mm nominal diameter, sloped parallel to stair pitch or stringer, minimum height 1100 mm at landings, meeting local code requirements.
Infill at picket railings shall consist of 12.5 mm square solid steel vertical bars at maximum 100 mm centers, welded to top and bottom rails.
Infill at pipe railings shall consist of 50 mm nominal diameter pipe or tube rails sloped parallel to stair pitch, welded and ground smooth.
End and intermediate guard posts shall match top rail material and size, spaced at maximum 1.5 m on center, welded to top surface of stringer.
All external stair, ramp and handrail installations and associated components shall be factory prefinished for C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012.

Stair and railing joints may be welded or bolted provided they meet the specified commercial quality level; where site welding is restricted, concealed couplings with rivets may be used subject to A/E review.

Fixed ladders associated with stairs shall use standard steel tubes, plates, bars, shapes, sheet, wire and mesh; rails shall be steel flats, guardrails 1100 mm high; rungs 20–50 mm rectangular steel, maximum 600 mm clear width, vertical spacing 225–300 mm with maximum 6 m between landings.

Fixed ladder landings shall be open grid or expanded metal with self-closing trap doors; guarding shall include circular flat steel plate safety cage hoops up to maximum 3 m above floor where specified.
Fixed ladder and associated rails/guards shall be galvanized in factory post-fabrication.

finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: Sa 2.5 to EN ISO 8501-1; EN ISO 8503-1; EN ISO 8502-3; EN ISO 8503-2
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Steel surfaces shall be blast cleaned to Sa 2.5 (ISO 8501-1) using dry blasting from initial rust grades A or B; abrasives must be of suitable type and size, free from fines, water and oil; all abrasive residues and surface defects detrimental to protective paint systems shall be removed; blast cleaning shall only be performed when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3°C above dew point; after blasting, all traces of dust and residues shall be removed and surfaces kept uncontaminated, with workers handling blast-cleaned steel wearing clean gloves; surface profile and roughness shall comply with EN ISO 8503-1/-2 and dust levels checked per EN ISO 8502-3 where required.

finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: NBN EN ISO 12944-1; NBN EN ISO 12944-2; NBN EN ISO 12944-5; NBN EN ISO 2808
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Corrosivity classifications for steelwork shall follow NBN EN ISO 12944-2 with internal steelwork treated for C2 environments and external steelwork for C4 environments unless otherwise stated; corrosion protection to all primary steelwork shall comply with NBN EN ISO 12944; the Contractor shall submit corrosion protection proposals including durability ranges (L to VH) in accordance with NBN EN ISO 12944-1; shop coats shall be applied within four hours of cleaning and before rust bloom occurs; painting shall only occur when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3°C above dew point; during application, each coat thickness shall be checked using wheel or comb gauge in accordance with NBN EN ISO 2808; coating systems shall be free from defects such as slumping, cracking, flaking, blistering, and must maintain appearance and performance throughout the specified service life under all environmental conditions.

finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: Fabricator’s standard rust-inhibitive primer; inorganic zinc-rich primer; EN ISO 12944-5
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: All structural steel shall receive a shop coat of rust-inhibitive primer except members encased in concrete, contact surfaces of welded connections and adjacent 50 mm of field welds, contact surfaces of slip-critical high-strength bolted connections, surfaces receiving sprayed or intumescent fireproofing where a compatible heavy duty alkyd primer shall be used, and surfaces for field welded studs; members exposed externally outside a controlled building environment shall be primed with an inorganic zinc-rich primer having minimum 60% volume solids and at least 85% metallic zinc in the dry film; primers shall be applied to cleaned surfaces, with DFT controlled and verified; shop primer for metal fabrications shall be a grey metal primer applied to minimum 50 microns DFT; surfaces in direct contact with concrete or requiring site welding shall not be primed.

All cutting, drilling and welding shall be completed before galvanizing; design of fabrications shall minimize risk of distortion and allow for proper drainage and venting; necessary vent and drain holes of correct size shall be provided in approved locations and sealed to approval after galvanizing; structural steel members, ladders, barrier rails, ledge/shelf angles, concrete edge confinement angles, downpipe guards, canopy supports, and external stair and railing components shall be hot-dip galvanized after fabrication to meet EN ISO 1461 requirements; design shall follow EN ISO 14713-1 guidelines for corrosion resistance and detailing; where there is concern about distortion of large articles, they should be single dipped where possible, or the structure spliced to permit single dipping.

The finish on external steel structures shall satisfy a ‘bright, light surface’ requirement for relative absorptivity in accordance with NBN EN 1991-1-5; all external and exposed metal fabrications, stairs, ramps, handrails and associated components shall be prefinished in factory to a corrosion protection level suitable for C4 environments, conforming to EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Intumescent Fireproofing – Sherwin Williams FIRETEX Systems
finishes_and_protection.environment_class: C1 internal steelwork (with provision for C2, C3, C4 by design)
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN 16623; EN 13381-4; EN 13501; EN ISO 12944-5; Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003; FIRETEX FX6002; FIRETEX C69; FIRETEX M71V2
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Steel members to receive intumescent coatings shall be blast cleaned to required standard (typically Sa 2½ per EN ISO 8501-1) and primed with an approved compatible primer; System 1 uses FIRETEX FX2003 intumescent basecoat with FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer (nominal 25 microns DFT per EN ISO 12944-5) and FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish topcoat (nominal 50 microns DFT per EN ISO 12944-5); System 2 uses FIRETEX FX6002 ultra fast drying intumescent basecoat with the same primer and topcoat system; DFT of intumescent basecoat shall be determined from EN 13381-4 test data and manufacturer’s assessment to meet required fire resistance; under certain conditions, FX2003 may be applied directly to steel blast cleaned to Sa 2½ with 50–100 micron profile, subject to manufacturer approval; all coatings shall be applied strictly per manufacturer’s technical datasheets and method statements, under controlled ambient conditions for temperature, humidity and ventilation, and be protected from rain, sunlight, high humidity, and wind-borne contaminants during application, drying and curing; primers must be fully cured before application of intumescent; top sealer shall be applied after basecoat achieves required DFT and is fully cured.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Shop Finishing – Metal Stairs, Ramps, Handrails and Guards
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN ISO 1461; EN ISO 12944-2; ISO 9223; EN ISO 17463
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Before finishing, all metal stair and handrail surfaces shall be cleaned of rust, scale, grease and foreign matter; surfaces in direct contact with concrete and areas requiring site welding shall not be primed; one coat of grey metal primer or approved equal shall be applied as shop and touch-up primer to minimum 50 microns DFT where painting is specified; all galvanized components shall be hot-dip galvanized to EN ISO 1461; abraded areas after fabrication shall be touched up using a specified primer compatible with galvanized surfaces and anticorrosive performance verified per EN ISO 17463; all external stair, ramp and handrail installations shall be factory-prepared to a finish suitable for C4 environment in accordance with EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Structural Steel Fabrication and Erection – Execution Class
tolerances_and_rules: All structural steel used on the project shall be designed, fabricated and erected in Execution Class 2 (EXC2) as defined by NBN EN 1090-2 unless noted otherwise on A/E drawings.
Fabrication and erection shall comply with all relevant EN codes including national annexes, complementary standards and national best practice documents for steel buildings and bridges.
Steel erection must meet the requirements of EXC2 including workmanship, inspection and testing obligations defined in NBN EN 1090-2.
Align, level, adjust and plumb individual members of the structure within EN 1090 tolerance limits; setting out and construction tolerances shall be considered absolute and not additive.
Level and plumb individual members in final position within EN 1090 tolerances; splice members only at locations indicated on drawings or subsequently agreed and accepted on shop drawings.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Structural Steel Connections – Design and Detailing
tolerances_and_rules: Connections shall be designed and detailed to resist loads and reactions shown in the design documents and not less than robustness requirements of NBN EN 1991; eccentricity effects shall be properly accounted for.

Beam-to-column connections shall minimize eccentric loading on columns; simple unrestrained beam end connections shall be detailed and fabricated to minimize or eliminate end restraint, with welds, bolts and connection material designed for eccentricity.

Beams shall be designed for end shear reactions indicated on design documents; bracing connections shall be designed for forces shown; all member connections shall be designed for actions shown in project documents.
Except for moment connections and bracing, provide bearing-type high-strength bolted assemblies; bearing connections shall be designed assuming threads included in the shear plane.
Moment and bracing connections shall be slip-critical with installation using direct tension indicators or tension-control bolted assemblies per manufacturer’s written instructions.
Members forming bracing systems or lattice girders shall be positioned so lines of action of axial forces intersect at a common point unless detailed otherwise.
All shop and erection connection details shall be prepared under supervision of the Contractor’s Engineer in accordance with NBN EN 1993.
The contractor shall design and provide stiffeners, doubler plates, reinforcing plates and their connections as necessary to achieve force transfer and connection criteria in Contract Documents.
All forces shown on structural drawings shall be treated as reversible unless expressly noted otherwise and connections must be checked for both load directions.
Where no forces are shown, the most critical combinations of member forces and directions shall be assumed for connection design.

For high restraint welds, use double bevel joints in preference to single bevels where practical; detail joints to allow for weld shrinkage; for plate intersections in more than one plane, show welding sequence on drawings and generally commence welding at most restrained parts progressing to least restrained.
All connection notes on drawings must be followed concurrently with specification requirements.
Calculations for all connection designs shall be submitted before preparation of shop drawings.

Each calculation shall be numbered in a logical and orderly manner; once submitted, calculations shall not be renumbered; resubmitted calculations shall retain the same number with an 'R' suffix, and all changes shall be clouded.
Alternative numbering protocols may be imposed by project BIM Execution Plan or other project documents and shall be followed when instructed.

Provide sketches with each calculation showing all pertinent dimensions (pitch, gauge, edge distance, unbraced lengths, Whitmore length and force spread in gussets) accurately to scale; sufficient sketches shall be provided to cover the full range of geometric conditions.
For repetitive connections, provide a spreadsheet or computer program summary table for each specific location along with a representative standard calculation demonstrating methodology.
Provide drawings showing overall locations of connections keyed or referenced to each connection calculation.

Calculations shall be typed or prepared using spreadsheets or computer programs as approved by the Engineer of Record; spreadsheets shall show inputs and results for all calculation steps with explanatory text and sketches describing assumptions.
Provide full calculation checks for all forces indicated on drawings; all NBN EN 1993 code requirements apply and 'OK by inspection' is not permitted.
All connection design and detailing remains the responsibility of the fabricator’s engineer even after review and comment by the Engineer of Record.
Shop fabricate structural steel to the greatest extent possible to minimize field assembly and splicing.

Submit details of proposed methods for identifying and recording materials and components; marking locations shall remain visible after erection but not placed on finished faces exposed to view, subject to Architect’s approval.
Fabricate for a delivery sequence that facilitates erection and minimizes field handling.
Complete assembly, including all welding, prior to commencement of finishing operations; finished surfaces of members exposed in final structure shall be free of markings, burrs and defects.
Shop connections shall be welded or bolted as indicated; field connections shall be bolted unless welded or other types of connections are specifically indicated.

High-strength threaded fasteners shall be used for principal bolted connections; unfinished bolts shall be used only for secondary members (purlins, girts and members taking nominal stresses) and temporary bracing.

High-strength bolted construction shall be installed in accordance with NBN EN 14399 and NBN EN 15048, with bolts installed with hardened washers under the element turned during tightening to aid verification inspection.
Built-up sections shall be assembled and welded using methods that ensure true axial alignment without warp.

Holes for other works shall be cut, drilled or punched perpendicular to metal surfaces; flame-cut holes or enlargements by burning are not permitted; bearing plate holes shall be drilled and resulting burrs removed.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Structural Steel Erection – Procedures and Temporary Stability
tolerances_and_rules: The contractor is responsible for analysis of all structural components and assemblies for stresses and displacements due to fabrication, shipping, handling, erection, temporary conditions and construction loads until the permanent structural system is complete and fully connected.

Prior to steel erection, the contractor shall verify by accurate survey the location, alignment and elevation of anchor rods provided by others and report discrepancies to Design Professionals; erection shall not commence until any required corrective measures are completed.

At least 20 working days before steel erection, the contractor shall hold a pre-erection conference with all relevant parties to review detailed erection requirements, including procedures, survey milestones, sign-offs and safety responsibilities; SER is not responsible for site safety programs.
Anchor bolt alignment, elevations, projections and sizes shall be accurately confirmed prior to erection of the superstructure; any inaccuracies or defects shall be reported immediately.
Erect structural steel in compliance with local best practice guidance and in accordance with NBN EN 1090 for bolted assemblies.
Allow for erection loads and provide sufficient temporary bracing to maintain the structure in a safe condition, plumb and in true alignment until permanent bracing is installed.

Structural frames shall be set accurately to the lines and elevations indicated; members forming part of complete frames shall be aligned and adjusted before permanent fastening; all bearing and contact surfaces shall be cleaned before assembly.
Splices shall only be located as indicated on drawings and accepted on shop drawings or as subsequently agreed with the Engineer of Record.
Holes in members shall not be enlarged by burning or use of drift pins; holes needing enlargement shall be reamed.

Gas cutting torches shall not be used in the field for correcting fabrication errors in structural framing unless approved by the Engineer of Record; where allowed, gas-cut surfaces shall be finished to resemble a sheared edge.
Field cutting or alteration of structural members is prohibited without prior approval of the Engineer of Record.
Erection must consider a minimum unrestrained temperature T0 = 10°C; steel erection practice shall ensure that this assumed temperature condition is satisfied during construction.
After erection, welds, abrasions and unprimed surfaces shall be primed except surfaces to be in contact with concrete.
Steel deck shall be installed in accordance with manufacturer’s written recommendations, approved submittals and specification requirements.
Metal deck units shall be positioned on supporting steel and accurately aligned to final position with units bearing tightly on top of supporting members.
Minimum bearing length of deck on steel support members shall be 50 mm.
Minimum roof deck end laps shall be 50 mm.
Cuts in decking shall be neat and trim; decks shall be cut using metal saws, drills or cutting torches, ensuring notches fit around columns and similar fabrications.
Field holes and openings shall only be cut where indicated on structural drawings and on approved submittals.

Provide metal closures for deck openings 1.58 mm wide and over, including cover plates for panel edges and changes of direction, column closures, sheet metal collars around service penetrations, and ridge/valley plates necessary to provide an acceptable surface for roofing.

No opening shall be cut in metal decking unless shown on approved submittals or specifically approved in writing by the Engineer of Record; for new openings not on approved submittals, modified shop drawings and calculations must be submitted and approved.
Burning or weakening of deck material around welds is grounds for rejection; deficient welds must be repaired or removed and replaced.

Composite deck fastening: provide 20 mm diameter puddle welds at each end and intermediate supports of deck units with maximum average spacing of 300 mm across width; puddle welds are not required where headed shear studs are welded through the deck.

For composite deck, longitudinal edges and side laps supported by steel members shall be fastened with 20 mm puddle welds at maximum 300 mm spacing along the panel length; unlapped edges without steel support shall be welded or fixed with self-tapping screws (minimum size as specified) at maximum 150 mm spacing between supports; longitudinal edge closures shall be tack-welded at maximum 600 mm spacing; sheet metal screws shall not be used for closures.

Non-composite deck fastening: similar puddle welds of 20 mm diameter at ends and intermediate supports with maximum average spacing of 200 mm across width; edge welds at maximum 300 mm spacing; side laps without steel support welded or screwed at maximum 150 mm spacing; edge closures tack-welded at maximum 150 mm spacing; sheet metal screws prohibited at closures.
Alternative mechanical anchoring systems such as Hilti or approved alternative may be used if supported by submitted and approved diaphragm design calculations.

Welding of shear studs through the deck into supporting beams shall only be carried out by welders certified by a recognized local authority; beams shall have clean top surfaces free of mill scale, rust, grease, oil, paint or other detrimental substances; flanges must be cleaned before laying decking; stud welding shall not be performed when ambient temperature is below 0°C.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Metal Fabrications – General Fabrication and Tolerances
tolerances_and_rules: Metal fabrications shall be formed from materials of size, thickness and shape indicated but not less than needed to meet performance requirements; dimensions shall match those indicated or accepted on shop drawings and use proven fabrication and support details.
Exposed work shall be formed true to line and level with accurate angles, surfaces and straight sharp edges.
Metals shall be sheared and punched cleanly and accurately; burrs shall be removed.

Exposed edges shall be eased to approximately 1 mm radius unless otherwise indicated; bent-metal corners shall use the smallest radius possible without causing grain separation or impairing performance.
Sharp or rough areas on exposed traffic surfaces shall be removed.
Corners and seams shall be continuously welded according to EN 1011 recommendations, producing hairline joints flush and smooth on exposed faces with concealed fasteners preferred.
Anchorage provisions shall be fabricated to type and spacing indicated to provide adequate support and secure connection to the supporting structure.
Shop assembled units shall be clearly marked for reassembly and coordinated installation on site.
Miscellaneous metal work shall be cut, reinforced, drilled and tapped as necessary to receive finish hardware and accessory components.
Joints exposed to weather shall be fabricated to exclude water, or weep holes shall be provided where water may accumulate.
Anchorage components shall generally be made from the same material and finish as primary fabrications unless noted otherwise.

For items to be galvanized, design shall minimize risk of distortion, use hot-rolled rather than cold-formed sections where possible to reduce internal stresses, avoid excessive jigging prior to welding, minimize size and amount of welds, and use balanced welding procedures.

Design shall incorporate appropriate vent holes of correct size for galvanizing and consider single-dipping of large articles; where single-dipping is not possible, consider splicing structures to permit it.

Fabrication tolerances for metal fabrications shall include: maximum difference in diagonal measurements (squareness) 3 mm; maximum offset between faces 2 mm; maximum misalignment of adjacent members 2 mm; maximum bow 3 mm in 1200 mm; maximum deviation from plane 2 mm in 1200 mm.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Metal Stairs, Ramps, Handrails and Guards – Execution
tolerances_and_rules: Stair assemblies shall be fabricated accurately for integration with the building structure and with one another, maintaining commercial-quality joints and finishes.
Fabricate pipe handrails and railing systems with member sizes, wall thicknesses, post spacing and anchorage adequate to support prescribed structural loads and compliant with design requirements.

Interconnect railing members by butt welding or internal connectors unless otherwise indicated; tee and cross intersections shall be mitered to match mating pipe contours and welded all around, or use concealed couplings with rivets where welding is restricted and A/E approves.
Changes in rail direction shall be formed by prefabricated flush elbows, specified radius bends, flush radius bends or direct bending as appropriate for the required configuration.
Simple and compound curves shall be formed by bending pipe in jigs to maintain uniform curvature and cross-section without buckling, twisting or cracking.
Provide wall returns at ends of wall-mounted handrails unless otherwise indicated; handrails shall extend beyond first and last nosings as required by local codes.
Exposed ends of pipe shall be closed by welding 2 mm thick steel plates in place or by prefabricated end fittings.
Drain or vent holes in pipes shall be located in inconspicuous positions and plugged prior to delivery to site.

Brackets, flanges, fittings and anchors shall be provided for connection of handrails and railing systems to structure; inserts and other anchorage devices shall be furnished for connections to concrete or masonry.
On site, components shall be installed plumb and level, free from distortion or defects, with sufficient temporary bracing to maintain true alignment until all permanent attachments are completed.
Field welding of stair and railing components shall comply with EN 1011; welded joints exposed shall be ground smooth and flush.
Site joints not specifically indicated as welded may be welded or bolted provided they achieve the required jointing quality level.
After erection, welds and areas not shop primed or galvanized shall be primed, except surfaces to be in contact with concrete.
When installing pipe railings and handrails, posts shall be spaced as indicated or as required by design loads, set plumb, and anchored to steel by welding to supporting members.
Handrail ends shall be anchored into concrete and masonry with steel round flanges welded to rail ends and secured with drilled-in expansion anchors.

Wall brackets for handrails shall provide minimum 50 mm clearance from inside face of handrail to finished wall; brackets shall be secured using concealed threaded hanger bolts, drilled-in expansion anchors for concrete/solid masonry, or direct fastenings to steel framing using self-tapping screws for steel-framed gypsum assemblies.
Maximum variation from plumb for installed elements shall be 6 mm; maximum offset from true alignment shall be 6 mm.
Interior and exterior stairs and railings shall generally receive galvanized finish.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Intumescent Fireproofing – Application and Quality Control
tolerances_and_rules: Prior to intumescent fireproofing works, a pre-construction conference shall be held at least 14 days before application to review quality control, construction requirements, submittals, material availability, scheduling, inspections, testing and reporting procedures.
Intumescent coatings shall be installed in accordance with manufacturer’s written instructions and technical literature, reflecting conditions of fire tests and assessments.

Enclosures shall be provided as needed to confine spraying, protect the environment and maintain adequate ambient conditions for temperature, humidity, air quality and ventilation during application and curing.
Substrates shall be cleaned of oil, grease, rolling compounds, incompatible primers, rust and mill scale prior to priming and intumescent application.
Primers applied to steel shall be compatible with intumescent coatings and fully cured before basecoat application; existing compatible shop primers may be used if in satisfactory condition.

Intumescent coatings shall be protected from rain, direct sunlight, high humidity and strong winds with dust or sand during application, drying and curing, except where test evidence supports alternative conditions.
Additional intumescent coats shall not be applied until the previous layer is fully cured.

Primer DFT shall be applied per manufacturer’s recommendation and EN ISO 12944-5; intumescent basecoat DFT shall achieve fire resistance ratings specified for each member; top sealer coat DFT shall follow manufacturer’s requirements and EN ISO 12944-5.

Independent testing agency shall perform field QC tests in accordance with Section 01 40 00, including verification of surface preparation standards (typically EN ISO 8501-1), surface profile (EN ISO 8503-2), contamination (EN ISO 8502-3), ambient conditions, batch identification, application timing relative to over-coating intervals, wet and dry film thickness checks and visual appearance against approved samples.

Dry film thickness measurements shall be conducted on primers and final coatings using systematic surveys on webs, flanges and faces of various section types; webs and flanges of I/T sections require two readings per meter per face; hollow sections and angles require two readings per meter per face; circular sections require eight readings per meter around the circumference.
For members shorter than 2 m, three sets of readings shall be taken (at each end and mid-length), each with the required number of measurements per face.

Acceptance criteria: average DFT on each element shall be at least the specified nominal value; average DFT on any face of any member shall be not less than 80% of nominal; DFT values less than 80% of nominal are acceptable only if isolated and not more than 10% of readings on a member; all DFTs must be at least 50% of nominal.

If any reading is below 80% of nominal, two or three additional readings shall be taken within 150–300 mm; if supplementary readings are all ≥80% of nominal, the initial reading may be treated as isolated; otherwise, further readings shall define extent of under-thickness areas, which must be brought up to required thickness before next application stage.
Average measured DFT of any face of any member shall not exceed the manufacturer’s recommended maximum for that section shape and orientation.

qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Contractor shall submit shop drawings for structural steel showing individual shipping pieces to be fabricated in the shop, including geometry, member sizes, connection details, and all information required for fabrication and erection; drawings shall be prepared and checked by a suitably qualified professional Structural Engineer; separate erection drawings and method statements shall show field installation and member placement, locations and details of all connections, and shall be coordinated with connection design calculations.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Temporary Works Drawings and Method Statements – Structural Steel
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Erector shall submit temporary works drawings and method statements illustrating erection sequence, all temporary supports, bracing locations, and detailed descriptions of bolting, welding and lifting operations; documents shall define sequence of work, locations of bracing, types and arrangement of temporary supports, and notes on connection and lifting procedures.

Contractor shall verify in writing within the submittal that structural steel contains 70 percent recycled content (pre- and post-consumer); a copy of this submittal shall be sent concurrently to EXE and DC Sustainability for tracking; if compliance is not possible due to availability, schedule or cost, contractor shall submit a written exception request to the Engineer of Record at time of submittal, with copies to EXE and DC Sustainability.

Design calculations for all structural steel connections shall be prepared under direct supervision of a Professional Structural Engineer and submitted before shop drawings; calculations must comply with NBN EN 1993 and associated national annexes, include reversible force checks, be fully documented with sketches and references to connection locations, and observe the numbering, revision and documentation controls defined in Section 2.1.C.10.

A Quality Plan for execution of structural steel works shall be prepared in accordance with NBN EN 1090 recommendations and submitted at the earliest possible time after appointment; all fabrication and erection work shall be carried out in accordance with this Quality Plan.

Manufacturer’s mill certificates shall be provided for structural steel products, certifying that all materials meet or exceed the specified mechanical grades and standards (e.g., NBN EN 10025, NBN EN 10210, NBN EN 10346).

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Welder Certificates – Structural Steel and Decking
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Certificates for all welders employed on structural steel and decking works shall be submitted, verifying qualifications in accordance with NBN EN ISO 9606-1 (fusion welding of steels) and other relevant standards; qualifications shall be current within the previous 12 months and include records available for examination; welders performing decking and stud welding shall be qualified per European Welding Association standards and NBN EN ISO 14732 as applicable.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Association and CE Marking Confirmations – Structural Steel
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Contractor shall submit confirmation of membership of a national Constructional Steelwork Association or other relevant organization, and provide evidence of CE marking accreditation appropriate to the required Execution Class for the project (EXC2 for steelwork).

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Pre-construction and Pre-erection Conferences – Structural Steel
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Contractor shall organize a pre-construction conference at least 14 days prior to structural steel erection and a pre-erection conference at least 20 working days prior to steel erection; required attendees include Contractor, Construction Manager, Engineer of Record, Structural Steel detailer, fabricator, erector, roof deck contractor, testing and inspection agencies and others as listed; minutes shall be prepared and distributed within 5 working days; conferences cannot substitute for formal submittals or approvals and comments made shall not be deemed binding on the A/E of Record.

Decking shop drawings shall include type, identification mark, gauge, finish, locations, openings, dimensions, placement sequence, anchorage and lap details, accessories, welding data, power requirements and electrode types; welding symbols shall follow European Welding Association standards; drawings shall show locations of unframed openings (including those to be cut after concrete placement), deck closures, deck reinforcement and types/locations of inserts.
Product data shall be submitted for steel decking including deck profile characteristics, dimensions, structural properties and finishes for each deck type used on the project.

Calculations for steel decking shall be performed by or under the direct supervision of a Professional Engineer specializing in structural engineering, signed and sealed; calculations shall cover section properties for each deck type and gauge, slab edge and closure strips, and shall accompany shop drawings; review of calculations does not relieve the Engineer of responsibility for their design.

Welder qualification data for decking and stud welding shall be maintained and made available for review; welders shall be qualified by tests prescribed in European Welding Association standards or relevant standards; where stricter requirements are not indicated by codes, each welder shall prepare two specimens of each required weld type for inspection, testing and approval by the Inspection and Testing Agency before being permitted to weld on the structure.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Shop Drawings – Metal Fabrications, Stairs, and Guards
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Shop drawings for metal fabrications, stairs, ramps, handrails and guards shall indicate profiles, sizes, connection attachments, reinforcing, anchorage, fastener sizes and types, accessories, erection drawings, elevations and detailed views where applicable; welded connections shall be indicated with ISO 2553-compliant welding symbols including net weld lengths; stair and railing shop drawings shall bear the design engineer’s signature on each sheet.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Fabricator and Structural Designer Qualifications – Steel Fabrications and Stairs
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Metal fabrications and stairs shall be produced by fabricators with proven experience in similar projects and sufficient capacity to avoid delays; structural designers responsible for stair and railing design shall be Professional Engineers experienced in this work and licensed in the project jurisdiction.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Intumescent Fireproofing – Product Data and Test Evidence
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: For each intumescent coating system, contractor shall submit product data sheets and independent fire test reports in accordance with EN 13381-4, including assessment of test results defining required DFT for the full range of section sizes; assessments shall be issued via organizations subscribing to the Passive Fire Protection Federation guidance on fire test assessments; manufacturer shall provide certificates confirming compatibility of intumescent coatings with primers, adhesives and other surface coatings; a table or printout shall be provided showing steel section parameters versus DFT for each intumescent product to demonstrate compliance with specified fire rating requirements.

Installers of intumescent coatings shall be experienced, certified, licensed or otherwise qualified by the intumescent manufacturer; installers shall have been trained directly by manufacturer’s employees (not by distributors or agents) and shall demonstrate successful completion of comparable projects in scope and size via qualification data including project locations, scopes, values, completion dates and contact references.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Field Quality Control – Structural Steel and Decking
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: An independent testing agency shall perform field quality control tests for structural steel and decking per Section 01 40 00; for high-strength bolted connections, the contractor shall provide for testing and verification of field-bolted assemblies; all field-welded connections in structural steel and decking shall be visually inspected; failed tests require re-inspection at no additional cost or time to the Owner.

Independent testing agency shall carry out field inspections for intumescent fireproofing including checks on surface preparation (cleanliness, profile, dust), ambient conditions during application (air and substrate temperatures, humidity, dew point), product batch numbers, application times and over-coating intervals, wet film measurements and dry film thickness surveys at primer, intumescent basecoat and final coating stages; results shall be documented and compared to specified and manufacturer-recommended values, with any deviations corrected by additional application and re-measurement.
